summary: Photographers love it for its tactile dials, colours, sharp files and the fun of using it, in a body lighter than most full frame. The main complaint is autofocus that trails Sony, Canon and Nikon on moving subjects, followed by finish and build issues such as scratching paint and a plastic feel. Suits stills, travel and street more than sports.

Most photographers praise sticky, fast autofocus, strong low-light files and handling that suits long shoots, with good battery life, dual card slots and in-body stabilisation. Complaints are scattered: some find the colours dull or greenish, a few want more than 24MP for cropping, and the electronic shutter shows rolling shutter. Suits sports, wildlife and hybrid shooters.

Many wildlife and sports photographers like its crop reach, comfortable grip, good value and, for some, fast autofocus. The main complaint is inconsistent autofocus, especially in low light, clutter or fast bursts, and several sold it for a full-frame body. Rolling shutter with the electronic shutter and noisier low-light files than full frame also come up.

Photographers praise its sharp lens, high-resolution image quality, simple menus and build, and it is a favourite travel camera. Autofocus is the main complaint, weaker on tracking and moving kids, though firmware 4.0 improved it for many. Some find the 28mm too wide, the body big for a compact, or the JPEGs needing edits.

Photographers praise it for putting full-frame quality and good low-light performance in a very light, compact body at a fair price. Recurring downsides are small battery life, overheating in video, and a rubber grip that wears or peels. Some miss in-body stabilisation, and the small body can feel cramped. Suits travel and hobbyists.

Impresses most photographers with clean image quality, strong low light, good colours and a handy detachable screen. Overheating is the leading complaint, with shutdowns during long 4K clips, followed by firmware and build glitches and weak battery life. The missing webcam mode also disappoints some. Better for shorter clips than long recording.

Photographers love it for its small size, colours and film simulations, and many carry it everywhere. Autofocus is the biggest complaint, with owners coming from Sony or Canon finding it slow or unreliable for kids, low light and video, and the fixed lens limits some. A few mention build faults and battery life. Suits street and travel.

Photographers praise its deep grip, long battery life, colours straight out of camera and strong video features in a small body. Overheating in video and heat is the top complaint, followed by autofocus that lags rivals on fast subjects and build some find loose or flimsy. Suits hybrid and travel shooters more than action.

Photographers mostly praise its strong low-light 360 video, sharp image quality and replaceable lenses. Downsides are bulk and weight, awkward on helmets and bikes, some build failures, heating at 8K, and slow, laborious editing and software. Single-lens mode helps some but trails dedicated action cameras.

Photographers love it as a pocketable everyday camera with a sharp zoom lens, physical dials, a good viewfinder and pleasing Leica colours. Complaints centre on the high price for a small, older sensor that limits low light and cropping, slow start-up, and a few build faults such as dust in the lens or sensor. Suits casual travel and street.

Photographers value it for its build, battery life, USB-C charging, image quality and engaging rangefinder shooting. The main complaint is random freezing and lost or corrupted files, often improved by firmware updates or the right SD card, plus a magenta cast some find hard to edit. The rangefinder is hard for fast-moving subjects. Suits deliberate shooters.

Photographers love it mainly as a small, premium-feeling camera with interchangeable lenses and sharp, crop-friendly files, and many call it their favourite carry-around. Downsides include weak battery life, a small EVF and touchy eye sensor, no weather sealing, and cramped handling without a grip. A few report overheating or slow wake.

Photographers love its exceptionally sharp APO lens, rich image quality and simple, enjoyable handling in a compact fixed-lens body. Autofocus is the main complaint, with those coming from Sony or Canon finding it slow or unreliable on moving subjects, though firmware improved it. The 43mm view feels tight for crowds and kids. Suits street and portraits.

Photographers like it for fast, reliable autofocus, excellent low-light files and a retro, dial-driven design that is fun to shoot. The common complaint is weight and ergonomics: the shallow grip is awkward with larger lenses, so many add a grip, and a few sold it as too heavy or uncomfortable. The flip-out screen and few custom options also irk some.

Photographers praise it for superb subject-tracking autofocus in a compact body, with good battery life, strong high-ISO results and plenty of lens choice. The main downside is overheating in long 4K video. A few miss the third dial or joystick, find it barely smaller than full frame, or find the JPEGs only competent. Suits travel, wildlife and hybrid shooters.

Owners love the compact, solid rangefinder experience, bright viewfinder and detailed files, and many call it a favourite camera. The leading complaint is freezing plus firmware and SD card trouble, though many say it stopped after updates or a card change. Manual focus misses shots on moving kids, and the 60MP sensor is demanding. Suits slow, deliberate shooting.

Photographers see it as a cheap, light way into full frame, with good low-light results and lovely stills for portraits, landscapes and travel. Common drawbacks are weak battery life, older autofocus and slow burst that struggle with sports, wildlife and video, and a few report poor build. Suits slower subjects on a budget.

Photographers praise it for being tiny and light with good image quality and colours, making it a popular everyday and travel camera, often with a pancake lens. The most common regret is the missing viewfinder, hard to live with in bright sun, and some find it cheaply built or cramped to hold. Suits casual carry or second-body use.

Photographers like it for its tiny magnetic hands-free design and good daylight quality, with better low light than the GO 3S for some. The main complaints are poor battery life, notably the detached camera draining while idle, plus overheating, and a few units dying after sitting or being lost off the magnetic mount. Dim-light footage is mixed.

Photographers like it as one of the smallest full-frame cameras, with autofocus many call near automatic, strong image quality and good low light. It is popular for travel and hiking with small primes. Downsides are few: some find it front-heavy with big lenses, miss a bigger grip, buttons or viewfinder, and the single card slot worries some.

Most owners love the hybrid viewfinder and hidden rear screen, and many call it their favourite camera for slow, deliberate shooting. The main complaint is fragility: the screen, its cable and the shutter button fail for a good number of owners, though many report years of trouble-free use. Best for those who rarely need the screen.

Most owners rave about the autofocus, pre-capture and high resolution, especially for sports, wildlife and cropping, and many upgraded from older Canon bodies. Downsides are mixed: video is criticised by several (heat, weak 60fps), battery life is short, and a few report build or colour disappointments.

Most owners love how small and light it is, and many say it became their travel or everyday camera, with good image quality, film simulations and stabilisation. The main complaint is autofocus, which some find misses moving kids and pets. A few mention a fragile feel, short battery life and fiddly handling for large hands.

Many owners value it for video, colour and custom modes, and some shoot sports and weddings on it happily. Autofocus splits opinion: a good number report missed shots on action and wildlife, and some sold it over that, while others find it fast and reliable. A few mention overheating, and it is bulky for travel.

Most owners praise the high-resolution image quality, colours, custom modes and solid build, and many use it for wildlife and professional work. Autofocus is the split: some lose shots or sold it, while others find it fine after firmware updates. It is big and heavy for travel and street, and a few report build faults.

Most owners call it an excellent all-round workhorse, with fast tracking autofocus for birds and action, a blackout-free viewfinder and a handy sensor shield. It is big and heavy, battery life is short for some, and a few report heat warnings or freezes. Many came from DSLRs or other brands and have no regrets.

Most owners praise the small, light body, good image quality for the money and strong autofocus, and it is popular as a first, travel or second camera. The main complaint is build reliability: several report mode dial, shutter or power switch failures. The tiny grip also bothers some large hands, and a few note overheating in video.

Most owners enjoy it as a tiny, fun, film-like pocket camera for casual shooting. The main complaint is that it is overpriced for what it delivers: image quality is only fair, weaker indoors and in low light, and a few found the build cheap. It suits fun snapshots rather than serious work.

Owners like the improved low light, 10-bit and I-Log footage, and the smaller body, though some see little difference from the X5 in daylight. The main complaints are build and software: the battery door, cover and USB storage give trouble for several, and many find the app, AI Director and firmware rough.

Most owners are happy with the stabilisation, battery, colours and handling, and many report years of reliable use in rough weather. Two complaints recur: autofocus that misses on action, birds and kids, and build problems such as paint wear, shutter or screen cable faults. Better for stills, video and slower subjects than fast action.

Most owners praise the autofocus, image quality and low light, and many switched from Fuji or Canon happily. The main complaint is overheating on long video and streaming, though several never see it. A few report shutter failures after heavy use, and some find the colours dull.

Most owners like the light, compact body with a good grip and real controls, strong autofocus and great value, and it works well for beginners, travel and as a light second body. Downsides are no stabilisation or weather sealing, weak low light with the kit lens, and a plasticky feel and short battery for some.

Most owners love the small, light body, colours and film simulations, and it is popular as a first, travel or everyday camera. Complaints are autofocus on moving subjects, short battery life and a cheap or small feel for some, plus no stabilisation. A few see overheating in video.

Still loved by most owners years on for its autofocus, low light and reliability, and many use it for paid work. The main complaint is the shutter, which several report failing after heavy use. Others dislike the dated menus and tilt-only screen, and a few never warmed to its handling.

Most owners love the autofocus, high resolution and cropping room, and many see no need to upgrade, including those using adapted EF lenses. Downsides are short battery life and heat in video, and a few report shutter or error problems. Several struggle with colours or white balance.

Most owners praise the autofocus, pre-capture, resolution for cropping and strong video, and many upgraded happily from older Canon or other bodies. Several find high-ISO noise slightly worse than the R6 Mark II, and a few find it big or note some heat. It suits action, wildlife and hybrid shooters.

Fans like the image quality, low light, stabilisation and small size, and some use it happily for street, travel and motorcycle POV. Reviews are split on photos and colour, which some find over-processed. Battery life is short, and several report waterproofing or build failures.

Owners like how light and compact this 360 camera is, which suits helmets, cycling, skiing and travel in good light. Its weakness is low light and grainy footage, and several find the file handling and editing frustrating. A few report connection or build faults.

Most owners praise the AI autofocus, pre-capture and fast burst for sports, birds and video, and many upgraded happily from the a7 IV, a7 III or APS-C. A handful report missed focus on fast subjects or late pre-capture. Some upgraders see little image difference, and full frame is bulky for travel.

Most owners are delighted, praising the fast autofocus, low light, handling and value, often after moving from a Nikon DSLR or Fuji. Battery life is shorter than a DSLR's, and a few report missed focus on moving pets. Several say it performs close to pricier Nikon bodies.

Most owners praise the fast autofocus, comfortable grip, excellent viewfinder, low light and video, and some call it a smaller Z8. A few find tracking hunts or locks onto the wrong thing, and some find it heavy or complicated. Several moved from older Nikon bodies.

Most owners like this light, compact APS-C body, whose subject-detect autofocus works well on birds and action for the price. Common gripes are no stabilisation, a small viewfinder and grip, weaker low light and shorter battery life. It works well with the kit zoom and adapted lenses.

Most owners love the low light, autofocus and ergonomics, and many keep it for years of event and wedding work, finding no need to upgrade. A few report shutter or power switch failures, and some find the colours uninspiring or the resolution limiting. It can overheat on long video.

Most owners love it for image quality, intuitive dials and durability, and many see no reason to upgrade after years in rain, snow and dust. The main complaint is autofocus on fast subjects like birds, kids and dogs, which led several to switch systems. A few mention build wear and no stabilisation.

Most owners love the small, light full-frame body, high-resolution detail and AI autofocus, and it suits travel, hiking and street. Some note huge files, a poor or small viewfinder, no joystick and a single card slot. A few report weak weather sealing and some are not fully sold on the autofocus.

Owners are very happy with the Sony a7R VI, mostly for its fast, confident autofocus on birds and wildlife, its 30fps electronic shutter and high resolution for cropping. Rolling shutter rarely bothers them. Downsides are minor: large files, some weight, and a little more noise than an a7 IV at high ISO.

Photographers praise the GoPro MAX2 for sharp 360 video in good light, its toughness, battery life and fit with existing GoPro accessories. Weak points are noisy, soft footage on overcast days or at night, plus some reports of overheating and build problems such as lenses that repel water poorly and a wobbly mount. Best in bright sun.

Photographers love the Lumix S9 as a small, light full-frame camera for travel, street and handheld video, with strong stabilisation, good autofocus and great straight-out-of-camera results with LUTs. The main drawback is no viewfinder, which bothers some in bright sun. It also lacks a mechanical shutter and a hot shoe, and offers little grip.

Owners love the Sony RX100 VII as a pocketable camera with a long zoom, a pop-up viewfinder and good autofocus and video, popular for travel and concerts. A few find it fragile or slow to operate, and one thought it overpriced. Image quality is good for the size but shows noise when pixel peeping.

Owners who like the Leica M EV1 find it light and easier to focus than a rangefinder with fast manual lenses, using focus peaking and punch-in. The viewfinder is the main sticking point: serviceable at best, laggy in low light, and not good enough for moving subjects such as young children. Battery life is poor.

Long-term owners are fond of the Fujifilm X-T20 as a small, light travel camera with lovely colours and a viewfinder, still producing great photos years later. The main downsides are build quality, with a few reports of dial failure or damage after a fall, and a toy-like feel. Focus speed and high ISO are modest.

The Sony a7R III is remembered as reliable and enjoyable years after release, with owners reporting heavy shutter counts, weather use without problems and no urge to upgrade. It is considered best for landscapes and less ideal for fast wildlife. Several find it bulky for travel or not comfortable to hold.

Most Z9 owners praise its autofocus, which tracks fast and unpredictable subjects such as birds, dancers and sports, even in dim arenas. Battery life, dual CFexpress slots and durability also earn credit. The body is big and heavy to travel with, and one owner found the rubber peeling early. A few prefer an optical viewfinder.

Owners of the Sony a1 II mostly find it a superb action and wildlife camera, with strong autofocus, very good stabilisation, clean video and fast readout. Complaints are weaker battery life, high cost compared to an a7 IV with similar-looking images, and tracking that can still miss shots in busy scenes. Less of a gain for portraits or landscapes.

Owners love the Ricoh GR IV as a truly pocketable camera with a great lens and very good image quality, often shot far more than their larger cameras. The main downsides are weaker low light than bigger sensors, autofocus that is slower and quirky, and a fixed 28mm view that takes getting used to.

Owners enjoy the original Nikon Z6 for its image quality, light weight and everyday usability, and several kept it for years across travel and event work. The main complaint is autofocus, with out-of-focus shots, weak wide-area AF and tracking that does not suit sports. It also comes up short for those who dislike its viewfinder.

Photographers like the Nikon ZR mainly for video, with compact size, colour and a great rear screen, and some use it as a stills backup that matches other Nikon bodies. Several miss a viewfinder in bright sun, and a few find stills dynamic range weaker than video. Overheating appeared in some long high-resolution recordings, though others never hit it.

Owners remain fond of the Sony a6000 years after release as a small, inexpensive everyday and travel camera that is quick for street shooting, good in daylight and versatile with lenses. Its age shows in noise as ISO rises, limited colour controls and some bulk with the kit lens. A few dislike its colours or grip.

Owners love the Ricoh GR III as an everyday pocket camera for travel, with vibrant colour and a sharp lens, and many say it gets them shooting more. The main criticism is autofocus, which two owners found bad enough to sell or return. Others miss a viewfinder, weather sealing or a longer lens than the 28mm.

Owners find the Fujifilm X-H1 a sturdy, comfortable workhorse with great image quality, good stabilisation and one of the best viewfinders, and several use it professionally for years with no trouble. Autofocus is the main downside, with some reporting missed focus or slow tracking for wildlife. It is a bit large for daily carry.

Owners enjoy the Nikon Zfc as a light, fun, retro-styled camera with manual dials that is easy to carry and good for everyday shooting. Downsides are a plastic feel and ergonomics that put one owner off, weaker low light for some, and a poor app transfer.

Owners call the original Sony a1 a beast for birds, wildlife and sports, praising its very fast, sticky autofocus, 30fps electronic shutter and resolution for cropping. It requires CFexpress cards, and the cost is high, though several say it is worth it. Almost no criticism appears.

Owners like the Canon PowerShot G7 X Mark III as a pocketable camera with a bright lens, flip screen, good low light and nice video and photos. The main complaint is price, with several saying it is too expensive now. A couple found it only adequate, not far beyond a phone, or not as good as the PowerShot V1.

Owners are happy with the Fujifilm X100F, calling it a fantastic, reliable camera that is easy to carry, with good photos and little wear after years of use. Downsides are the fixed lens and a few faults, including battery drain, a stuck optical viewfinder and a costly repair after a fall.

Many owners find the Sony a7R IV a big step up in resolution and dynamic range, with a good EVF, and some have shot huge numbers of frames on it. The main downsides are autofocus that hunts in medium or low light and with long lenses, plus heavy, large files that made some find it unwieldy.

Photographers like the Lumix S5II as good-value full frame, with strong stabilisation, a good hybrid autofocus and fine output. The common drawbacks are size and weight, which some found too clumsy for travel, plus weak battery life, a viewfinder that feels poor, and mushy buttons. Adapted lenses did not work well for one owner.

Owners like the Fujifilm X-E3 as a small, light everyday camera with lovely JPEG colours, great with pancake lenses and easy to shoot one-handed. Some feel it is plastic or toy-like next to bigger Fujis, one had the rubber grip come off repeatedly, and autofocus is not great for one owner.

Owners praise the Fujifilm GFX100S II for superb image quality and colours, and several say it replaced their other cameras. It is not the best choice for fast action or birding, where autofocus lags behind Sony or Nikon. Two owners hit a repeated restart error, which is a worry for reliability.

Most owners love the Sony a7R V for its sharp high-resolution files, its EVF and the fully articulating screen, and many moved up from an a7 IV or a7R IV and call it a great upgrade. The big files need a capable computer. Fast action is the weak spot: rolling shutter and the frame rate frustrate sports and small-bird shooters.

Photographers love the Fujifilm X-T30 II for being small and light, with the Fuji colours, a good viewfinder and a pancake or compact prime making it an easy everyday and travel camera. The downsides are a tiny grip, weaker battery life and autofocus that a few find unreliable with moving subjects, plus no IBIS for video.

Owners of the Leica M11-D mostly love the screenless, film-like way of shooting and the image quality, and many say it has been trouble-free. It relies on a phone app for most settings, and some find the connection hit or miss. Battery life and slow wake-up bother a few, and a couple of owners had serious reliability faults.

Photographers praise the GoPro MISSION 1 PRO for far better low light and image quality than earlier GoPros, plus strong slow motion and log video. Downsides are common: overheating at high resolutions, heavy battery drain, and soft footage at distance because of a close minimum focus. Several also report build problems like cracked screens and freezes.

Overheating is the main complaint with the GoPro HERO13 Black: many owners report shutdowns in heat or long recordings, though a few never had it happen. Image quality is good in daylight and stabilisation is strong, but low light is weak and several switched to DJI. A few reported build faults such as seals and card errors.

Owners love the Fujifilm X-E4 as a slim everyday and travel camera, often with a pancake lens, and many say it is their favourite to carry. The main complaints are the lack of a grip, few buttons and no IBIS, so bigger lenses feel awkward. A few also found the build plasticky or fragile.

Owners of the Leica M11 Monochrom rave about the black and white image quality, detail and very clean high ISO, and enjoy its deliberate, film-like way of shooting. Most report no problems, but a few have had freezes, and one saw top plate paint fading. It is not the most practical camera.

Owners like the Fujifilm X-S10 for its deep grip, IBIS, flip screen and easy-to-carry size, and many have used it happily for years for both photos and video. Autofocus is the main complaint: a few found it poor for fast subjects or sold it over that. Some also dislike the button layout.

Photographers value the Canon PowerShot V1 mostly as a pocketable video camera, with reliable autofocus, a wide 16mm end, good stabilisation and built-in ND. Stills are good but a few find them soft. Battery life is short, there is no viewfinder, and small flashes need an adapter.

Owners praise the Fujifilm GFX100RF for its image quality, dynamic range and surprisingly clean high ISO, in a compact fixed-lens body that many grab as a daily camera. The f/4 lens and lack of IBIS limit low light for some, and a few questioned autofocus. Files are large.

Owners like the Sony a7C as a compact full-frame body with good image quality and autofocus that is easy to carry with small lenses. The tiny viewfinder is the main complaint, followed by a small grip. Some found it unbalanced with larger lenses, and a few sold it for something more enjoyable.

Most photographers see the Canon EOS R100 as a great-value, light entry camera that gives good photos and works well as a first or travel camera. Autofocus is the main weakness, especially for birds and moving subjects. Some also outgrow the fixed screen and limited controls.

Owners enjoy the Canon EOS R50 V as a small video-first camera, with good autofocus, C-Log3 and nice Canon colours that also gives good stills. The lack of a viewfinder is the most common gripe, along with hard-to-grip larger lenses. A few mention short battery life, overheating or poor buttons.

Many owners like the Nikon Z6II for low light, image quality and a lighter body, and happily moved to it from DSLRs. Autofocus is the main complaint: several find it struggles with moving subjects, video and backlit scenes. Opinions vary, with some calling it fine for stills.

Owners adore the Ricoh GR IIIx as a truly pocketable camera with sharp images, and many carry it everywhere. The main downsides are weak autofocus, short battery life and no viewfinder, and some find it demanding rather than point-and-shoot.

Owners love the Canon EOS R3 for its very fast, sticky autofocus, comfortable gripped body, custom buttons and huge battery, and it has proved tough in heavy use. Its size and weight bother a few, and the 24MP resolution limits cropping for some. A couple were underwhelmed by autofocus.

Owners like the Sony a6400 as a compact, well-priced camera with strong autofocus that has lasted for years. Complaints are a small grip, no IBIS and clunky menus and controls. Video gets mixed reviews.

Owners praise the Nikon Z7II for image quality at 45MP, build and compact travel setups with small lenses. Autofocus is the main complaint, with several calling it slower than newer bodies, though others get good results after tuning. It suits landscapes and slower work best.

Owners still like the Canon EOS R for its 30MP image quality, skin tones, battery and build, and many use it happily as a main body for portraits and landscapes. Autofocus is the main weakness, especially for sports and wildlife, and the touch bar bothers some. A few reported shutter failures.

Owners love the Fujifilm X-T2 for its handling, colours and solid feel, and many keep it despite owning newer bodies. Autofocus is dated for moving subjects like children and birds. A few had weather-related failures like jammed shutters after getting wet.

Photographers say the Nikon Z5 gives good pictures and good value, and several are happy with it for static or slow subjects. Autofocus is the dominant complaint: many found it unreliable for moving subjects and video, and some moved to a newer body.

Owners love the DJI Osmo Pocket 3 for its pocketable size, smooth stabilisation and good video quality, and use it for vlogs, B-roll and travel. It is delicate and not water resistant, and a few had battery or support problems. It handles heat better than some rivals, though one saw it drop resolution.

Owners are devoted to the Fujifilm X-Pro2 for its hybrid viewfinder, tactile dials and solid build, and many prefer it to newer Fujis. Few downsides come up, such as settings resetting on battery swap and not suiting pro work. One owner sold it over blurry photos.

Owners like the Fujifilm X100V for its look, portability and all-in-one simplicity. Main downsides are autofocus for moving subjects, no IBIS, and some report overheating in video and poor battery life. A few did not connect with it.

Owners enjoy the Nikon Z30 as a small, light camera for travel and hiking that also does good vlogging video. The missing viewfinder bothers some, and a few reported battery problems, overheating in long 4K video or missed focus.
